title: Traffic slice launch surgery and incident ownership handoff
topics: traffic slicing plan for beta launch
KV cache and prefix cache benching
oncall runbook handoff and escalation path
summary: Runbook and ownership for a staged traffic-slice launch. Agreed on 3-level fallback, who owns each rung, action to run KV/prefix cache bench with representative sequences, and security checklist for private VPC gating. Next: bench results, updated runbook, scheduled rehearsal with oncall.
next_steps: Samir to run KV/prefix cache benchmark across 4 sequence lengths and share sheet by 2027-08-10
Casey to update runbook with 3-level fallback matrix and pages for each owner by 2027-08-08
Jordan + Asha to schedule a 60m oncall rehearsal 2027-08-12
Ben to confirm SSO/KMS gating checklist and share secure link by 2027-08-06
action_items: Samir - KV/prefix bench (short, med, long, convo) - due 2027-08-10
Casey - write fallback ownership doc + links - due 2027-08-08
Jordan - add fallback metrics to dashboard (p95/p99 latency by slice) - due 2027-08-09
Asha - rehearsal facilitator + postmortem template - due 2027-08-11
Ben - security gate checklist for private deploys - due 2027-08-06
header:
Date: 2027-08-04 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62 mins | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees: Priya Nair, Jordan Lee, Samir Patel, Casey Rivera, Asha Gupta, Maya Thompson, Leo Wright, Ben Cho, Rina Alvarez
transcript:
[00:00:00] Priya (PM): All right, thanks everyone for hopping on. quick agenda 14 walk through the traffic slicing plan, confirm ownership of fallback rungs, and then go over security gating for the private beta. we'll try to keep this tight.
[00:00:18] Maya (VP Eng): Sounds good, Priya. a lot riding on this window so i want clarity on who does what if we see a token-cost spike or latency drift.
[00:00:32] Jordan (SRE): yeah, and to add, we've got two things: the runtime behaviors around KV cache warmup and the orchestration side where slices get moved between pools. those are separate failure modes.
[00:00:47] Samir (Runtime Eng): quick note on wording 14 KV cache sometimes gets transcribed as K V cash in logs so forgive any mismatch later, but basically cold cache will cost us both p95 and token-count. i've got some preliminary numbers but need the bench to be representative.
[00:01:05] Casey (Product): maybe start with the fallback rungs? priya, you proposed a three-level fallback in the doc 14 can we read that out and confirm owners?
[00:01:16] Priya: yeah, so level 1 is graceful degrade within the same model variant using prefix cache prioritization and short-circuiting heavy op paths; owner: runtime eng (Samir) with SRE alerting to Jordan. level 2 is route to a quantized compatible variant in the same region 14 owner: infra/runtime (Jordan + Samir). level 3 is cross-region fallback or burst to dedicated pool 14 owner: operations (Maya/Leo) and product ops for customer messaging.
[00:01:51] Asha (Oncall Eng): i have a question 14 for level 1, what's the exact SLO change? are we comfortable with increased p99 there? we need thresholds in the runbook.
[00:02:03] Jordan: good call. propose: trigger 1 when p95 latency > 600ms sustained for 2m and error rate > 0.5% in that slice. trigger 2 if p99 > 1.5s or token-cost per request jumps by 30% for 5m. these are draft.
[00:02:23] Ben (Security): on the security side, we need the KMS key usage audited during fallback if traffic routes to dedicated pools that use customer-managed keys 14 audit logs must be sent to the central SIEM. also SSO reauth flow shouldn't break during fallback.
[00:02:40] Rina (Product Ops): note: user messaging template exists but needs to be adapted per customer tier. Priya, can we add a template for internal customers vs external?
[00:02:53] Priya: yes, add both. okay, Samir, you said bench numbers 14 what's the plan to make the bench representative?
[00:03:02] Samir: plan is to run four sequence-length profiles: short (16 tokens), medium (128), long (1024), and convo-style (avg 300 with varying prompt prefix). we'll run against both cached-warm and cold states, and with the new kernel changes. i'll parameterize the batch sizes to mimic the production request distribution.
[00:03:28] Maya: make sure you include KV cache warming delay in the cold. last time the warm profile was optimistic.
[00:03:35] Samir: agreed. i'll also include a pass that sim's KV churn 14 repeated unique prefixes to force cache eviction.
[00:03:44] Casey: what about the observability hooks? jordan, do you need new traces or tags?
[00:03:50] Jordan: yeah, need two things: a slice tag on every request and a fallback-rung tag when we actually degrade. that way dashboards can be filtered. i'll add p95/p99 and cost-per-token for each slice.
[00:04:03] Asha: and an alert that only pages on rung-3; rung-1/2 should just go to slack ops channel to avoid noisy pages.
[00:04:09] Priya: agreed. rung-3 pages the oncall rotation. rung-2 is paged to the infra lead only if it escalates after 10m.
[00:04:20] Leo (Oncall Lead): to be clear, when rung-3 triggers and we failover to dedicated pool, what's our rollback window? are we automatic or manual?
[00:04:30] Jordan: automatic failover to dedicated pool but manual rollback. we don't want flip-flopping. there will be a cooldown of 15 minutes before an automatic rollback attempt.
[00:04:42] Maya: ok that seems sensible. next, security gating 14 Ben?
[00:04:48] Ben: checklist includes SSO/SAML verification, KMS key rotation policy compliance, SIEM audit stream, and confirm that private VPC peering handles egress rules. also we need to ensure that telemetry doesn't send PII.
[00:05:02] Priya: can you commit to a link to the checklist by Friday?
[00:05:06] Ben: yes i'll post the doc by 2027-08-06.
[00:05:09] (small crosstalk)
[00:05:20] Priya: back to the bench 14 Samir, what's your ETA?
[00:05:23] Samir: i can run a first pass within 48 hours but to get stable numbers i need the representative mix we talked about. if rina can provide traffic slice percent by sequence-length distribution, i can fold that into the bench weights.
[00:05:37] Rina: i can. i'll export the beta slice traffic from staging and share by EOD tomorrow.
[00:05:43] Priya: great. now, small sticky point: quantized variants. we do have quality regressions with some customer prompt sets. Casey, can you lead an eval to confirm quality windows where quantized variant is acceptable?
[00:05:57] Casey: yes, i will run an eval harness against the core prompt set plus 10 adversarial prompts. i'll mark any prompts that exceed our quality delta threshold (0.05 BLEU-ish proxy or model score).
[00:06:13] Maya: make sure the eval script includes reranking cases; quantization hit there is often worse.
[00:06:19] Samir: on the runtime side, i can instrument a quality-check stop-gap: if the quantized variant's output dev metrics drop by X, we can automagically fall back to exact variant for that customer. but that'll add cost.
[00:06:34] Jordan: and we should tie that to a customer tier. Enterprise customers should get strict guarantees, PLG gets cost-first fallbacks.
[00:06:43] Priya: agreed. add customer-tier matrix to the runbook.
[00:06:48] (background noise)
[00:07:00] Asha: rehearsal logistics 14 who will run the drill? Priya or Jordan?
[00:07:06] Priya: i'd like Asha to facilitate, Jordan to run the telemetry side, Samir as subject-expert on runtime. Rina will play product ops and send simulated customer messages.
[00:07:18] Asha: noted. i'll craft scenarios: slow ramp, sudden spike, and KV-thrash. each scenario will have a time-boxed checklist.
[00:07:27] Leo: for the drill, make sure the paging escalation is tested too 14 we need to validate rung-3 pages the right rotation.
[00:07:33] Jordan: will add synthetic load generator that marks a slice. hope to keep the rehearsal to 60 minutes.
[00:07:39] Priya: good. moving on 14 telemetry dashboards. what do we need as minimum?
[00:07:44] Jordan: per-slice p50/p95/p99, error rate, cost-per-req, fallback-rung counts, and KV hit-rate. also a small table with top prompt prefixes causing heavy token counts.
[00:07:58] Casey: can we auto-surface top-20 heavy prefixes daily so product can consider prompt-guidance?
[00:08:04] Samir: yes once we tag prefixes at ingress we can aggregate. beware of privacy 14 Ben, any concerns?
[00:08:11] Ben: prefix-level aggregation is fine if hashed and PII stripped. please consult the privacy checklist.
[00:08:18] Priya: okay. i want to capture a couple of open risks before we close: 1) KV eviction churn under real beta traffic might be worse than staging; 2) quantized variant regressions for edge prompts; 3) SSO flow break during cross-region failover. any others?
[00:08:37] Maya: supply-chain risk 14 a kernel fallback we depend on from upstream could land late. need contingency.
[00:08:44] Samir: yeah, i'll prepare a fallback patch that avoids the new kernel if we need to roll back quickly. not ideal performance-wise but safe.
[00:08:52] Priya: thanks. quick recap: Samir runs bench; Casey writes quality evals and runbook content; Jordan adds dashboards and alert rules; Asha runs rehearsal; Ben posts security gate; Rina shares slice distribution. deadlines as on the action items.
[00:09:09] Rina: can we also add a short post-rehearsal template for notes and owner sign-off?
[00:09:15] Asha: i'll add the template to the runbook and own the sign-off step.
[00:09:19] (brief pause)
[00:09:30] Priya: any last comments?
[00:09:32] Leo: one ask 14 include a brief appendix in the runbook showing rollback checklist and contact matrix.
[00:09:43] Maya: noted.
[00:09:46] Casey: just that we should document customer-facing SLAs for failover messaging. i'll draft templates.
[00:09:52] Priya: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after bench results. meeting adjourned.
[00:10:00] (recording stops)
notes: Bench must include eviction churn simulation
Runbook ownership matrix agreed (Samir/ Jordan/ Maya)
